combustionPumpIntro: Autolejek can stop an engine-driven pump automatically by using the engine's original on/off switch circuit, also known as a kill switch. The Autolejek relay reproduces the switch electrically by opening or closing its circuit at the appropriate time.
combustionPumpSwitchTestIntro: The measurement below shows how to determine whether a kill switch stops the engine by closing or opening its circuit. With the engine switched off and secured against accidental starting, set the multimeter to continuity mode (the diode or buzzer symbol) and test both the ON and OFF positions.
combustionPumpProbePointsText: The blue circles indicate where to place the multimeter probes.
combustionPumpSwitchOnAlt: Pump switch in the ON position during a continuity test, with probes touching the points marked in blue and the multimeter displaying OL
combustionPumpSwitchOnCaption: ON position: the multimeter displays OL, meaning no continuity. The kill-switch circuit is open and the engine can run.
combustionPumpSwitchOffAlt: Pump switch in the OFF position during a continuity test, with probes touching the points marked in blue and the multimeter displaying approximately 0.22 ohms
combustionPumpSwitchOffCaption: OFF position: the multimeter displays approximately 0.22 Ω, confirming continuity. The kill switch connects the wire to ground and stops the engine.
combustionPumpSwitchConclusion: On this pump, the engine is stopped by connecting the kill-switch wire to ground. Other models may work in the opposite way, so always test both switch positions before connecting Autolejek.
combustionPumpExampleContacts: For the arrangement shown, connect the kill-switch circuit wires to COM and NC on the Autolejek relay. While the system is running, the energised relay opens COM–NC and allows the engine to operate. When Autolejek stops or loses power, the relay releases, closes COM to NC, and stops the engine. Do not use NO with this operating logic.
combustionPumpRelayImageAlt: RELAY2 connector with COM, NC and NO contacts on the Autolejek controller board
combustionPumpRelayImageCaption: The RELAY2 connector on Autolejek provides COM, NC, and NO contacts.
combustionPumpRelayText: The correct connection depends on the pump design. Some engines stop when the kill-switch circuit is closed, while others stop when it is opened. A relay with COM, NC, and NO contacts can reproduce either arrangement.
combustionPumpContactsText: COM is the common contact. When the relay is de-energised, COM is connected to NC. When the relay is energised, COM–NC opens and COM connects to NO.
combustionPumpLogicWarning: Do not choose the contacts by guesswork. Consult the pump wiring diagram or test the kill switch with a multimeter. An incorrect connection may prevent automatic shutdown or stop the engine unexpectedly.
combustionPumpAdviceFirstText: Set the original pump switch to ON and start the engine. Then switch on Autolejek. Once its relay is energised, move the pump switch to OFF. The engine will continue running because the relay keeps the circuit open. Stopping Autolejek closes the circuit and stops the engine.
combustionPumpAdviceDelayText: You can switch on Autolejek first while leaving the pump switch in the OFF position. The energised relay opens the kill-switch circuit, allowing the engine to start. Configure a suitable startup period in Autolejek so minimum-flow monitoring begins only after the engine has started and the flow has stabilised.
combustionPumpOtherIntro: The method described above applies to a simple kill-switch circuit. Depending on its design, an engine may instead be stopped by:
combustionPumpElectronicInput: an electronic STOP input on an engine controller,
combustionPumpOpenCircuit: a switch that stops the engine by opening rather than closing a circuit.
combustionPumpSafetyText: Connect the relay only to the low-current original switch circuit and follow the pump manufacturer's wiring diagram. Verify that the current through the contacts does not exceed the Autolejek relay rating. Do not use it to switch a starter motor or another high-power load, and never connect it to the high-voltage spark-plug lead. Preserve a manual emergency-stop method and test automatic shutdown under controlled conditions before leaving the system unattended.
